ideas.description: Diagnostic with no recipe change. It feeds the frozen keep gate (H4.6) and also settles H4.4.3. Build the E049 tip (commit 3df6233) three times, each in a fresh process with its own private TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR. Run each build through the harness code path on fresh seeds 33–52 (benchmark.run --seed 33 --n 20) and on seeds 0–2. Record: per-seed accuracies for every build; the three 20-seed means; the per-seed differences between builds and their correlation across seeds; and mean time per build. Derive the rebuild SD σ_build of a 20-seed mean as the SD of the three means, after subtracting the expected per-seed-noise part (SD_seed/√20 × √2 for a difference). Also report E049's pooled fresh mean against its 0.7539 on reused seeds 13–32 (winner's curse, H4.4.3). Do not edit submissions/arena/. From now on, seeds 33–52 are the decision set and seeds 53–72 are reserved for one final confirmation per candidate.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (~5.20 s; builds within ~1% of each other). The 20-seed means of the three builds spread 0.03–0.20 pp (median range ~0.08), and per-seed build differences correlate positively, so σ_build ≈ 0.04–0.1 pp. E049's fresh mean is 0.7520–0.7545 (median ~0.7532), about 0.05 pp below its 13–32 reading. H4.4.3 is supported if the drop is ≥0.1 pp and refuted if within 0.05 pp. H4.5.1 is refuted if the build means differ by <0.04 pp.

ideas.description: Exploit plus a gate test. It may re-keep a faster recipe that has already been measured. Before reading any number, freeze the keep gate. Let μ̂ be a candidate's 20-seed mean on seeds 33–52. Let σ_tot = sqrt(SE20² + SD_seed²/40 + σ_build² + 0.05²), with σ_build taken from the H4.5.1 idea and 0.05 pp as the PCIe judge-drift term. Gate: μ̂ − 1.64·σ_tot ≥ 0.7500 (P(official ≥0.75) ≥ 0.95), and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 on the candidate's single committed build, with no rebuilding to chase a draw. Then build E052 (ce17ae7, 4.99 s) and E053 (f30d362, 5.07 s) once each in the same session as the H4.5.1 builds, and run each on seeds 33–52 and seeds 0–2. Pick the fastest candidate that passes. Confirm it once on reserved seeds 53–72, where it must pass the gate again, to undo the selection among candidates. Only then re-keep it, using its ar.py result from that one build. No recipe edits: both commits already exist.
ideas.expected: E052 fresh mean 0.7505–0.7535 (median ~0.7520). E053 0.7500–0.7535 (median ~0.7518). Deficit vs E049 on the same fresh seeds 0.05–0.25 pp (median ~0.13), smaller than on reused seeds 13–32 (−0.21/−0.24). With σ_tot ≈ 0.10–0.14 pp the gate threshold is ≈0.7517–0.7523, so E052 passes with ~45% probability. If it passes and is confirmed, the tip moves to ~4.99 s (−4%). If neither passes, the gate stays near 0.752 and is recorded as the frozen rule.

ideas.description: Re-measure the post-freeze epoch dial in the time-favourable direction, with no new code. E049 minus 0.25 true epoch is exactly E046 (commit 8a2452a: same group-2 freeze at 231 steps, all schedules as fractions). In the same session as the H4.5.1 builds, build E046 once and run it on seeds 33–52 and seeds 0–2. Compute dial = Δtime / Δacc against E049's builds on the same seeds, adding σ_build to the SE of the difference. Use the result to re-price every booster and cut, and to resolve the 0.7 vs 1.5 s/pp dispute in H4.2. E046 also enters the frozen gate as a candidate (it was feasible locally at 0.7540 / 5.08 s); if it is the fastest passing candidate, it goes through the 53–72 confirmation under the H4.6.1 idea's rule.
ideas.expected: Time −0.10 to −0.14 s vs E049 (E046 measured 5.08 s). Fresh 20-seed mean 0.06–0.20 pp below E049 (median −0.12), giving a dial of ~0.6–2 s/pp (median ~1 s/pp). A loss below 0.06 pp means the top-up in E049 bought nothing and E046 dominates E049. A loss above 0.2 pp means the post-freeze dial is steep (<0.6 s/pp), so the remaining cuts are all too expensive.

ideas.description: Explore, a time-neutral structural booster. Step 0: read RULES.md and the benchmark data loader. Run only if the 50k training set as shipped includes CIFAR-100 coarse labels (for example 'coarse_labels' in the train pickle). If the fine→coarse mapping would have to come from a hard-coded external table, treat it as external data, mark H1.8 blocked, and do not run. If allowed: in timed prepare, read the training coarse labels and build a 100×100 soft-target matrix T on the GPU. Each row gets 0.70 on the true class, 0.15 spread uniformly over all 100 classes, and 0.15 spread over the 4 other fine classes in the same superclass. Train with soft-target cross-entropy against T[y] in place of LS 0.3 (total smoothing mass unchanged). Warm up in build with a synthetic T of the same shape and dtype, with error_on_recompile on. Nothing else changes. Judge on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). 20-seed mean −0.10 to +0.25 pp vs E049 (median +0.05). A gain of ≥0.12 pp supports H1.8.1 and is worth ~0.1–0.2 s at the measured dial, which can be cashed in by a −0.25 epoch trim (the E046 step count). A change within ±0.05 pp closes H1.8, along with the last scalar-free booster family.

ideas.description: Fidelity check, code first. Read the port's BatchNorm setup. If every BN weight (scale) already has requires_grad=False (as in airbench96/Hiverge), close H1.5.10 with no run. If the port trains BN scale: on the E049 tip, set BN weight requires_grad=False at its init value of 1 in every BN layer, and remove those tensors from the SGD group and from Lookahead's averaged set. Keep the init RNG draw order unchanged. Recapture every resolution and step variant in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2, with per-step CUDA-event timing to separate the time effect from build noise.
ideas.expected: If the port trains BN scale: time −0.3 to −1.0% (fewer optimizer and fused-backward reads), and the 20-seed mean within ±0.1 pp (median 0). Keep if per-step timing shows ≥0.5% saved and the candidate passes the frozen gate. A loss of ≥0.15 pp refutes it: BN scale carries capacity in the 100-way short run.

ideas.description: Exploit, a near-free truncation. On the E049 tip, move the whitening-bias detach from 20% to 6% of steps (about step 14 of 237, inside the 20 px phase), with the whitening-bias LR annealed to 0 by 6% instead of 20%. The whitening-detached variants already exist at every resolution, so there are no new shapes; error_on_recompile stays on. Everything else is unchanged. Measure the saving with per-step CUDA-event timing (the expected effect is below the ~1% rebuild time spread) as well as wall time. Judge accuracy on seeds 33–52 against same-build E049, plus seeds 0–2. Consult the H7.1.1 curves if they are available first.
ideas.expected: Per-step timing shows −0.02 to −0.04 s per trial (−0.3 to −0.7%). Wall time 5.16–5.20 s. 20-seed mean within ±0.08 pp of E049 (median −0.02). Supported if the loss is ≤0.05 pp; then it is a free stackable cut. A loss of ≥0.12 pp means the bias adapts through the 20→24 px switch.

ideas.description: Explore diagnostic, offline, outside submissions/arena/. Instrument a copy of the E049 tip, run it on real data for seeds 33–35, and every 5 steps log ||ΔW||/||W|| for the whitening bias, group-1 convs, group-1 BN, group-2 convs, group-2 BN, group-3 convs, group-3 BN and the head, plus each group's gradient norm relative to its own peak. Mark the resolution switches, the LR peak, the anneal starts and the freeze points. Check whether the curves order the known outcomes: whitening bias below 10% of its peak rate by ≤10% of steps; group 1 only after ~70% (E028 free, E037/E054/E055 costly); group 2 only after ~88% (E046 marginal, E053 costly). Report the curves in the notebook.
ideas.expected: No change to the task metrics (time and accuracy are those of E049). Prediction: the whitening bias settles by ~5–10% of steps, and groups 1 and 2 cross the 10% threshold near 72–76% and 88–92%. If the curves place group 1's threshold before 60% (failing to separate E028 from E037), the learning-finished account is refuted as a predictor and freeze points must stay empirical.

structured_output.summary:
The cut-and-booster levers are close to exhausted: every per-step cut tried since E049 lost ≥0.2 pp on seeds 13–32. The decision that matters most now is the keep gate itself. It has drifted, it has never been tied to the official 40-seed ≥0.75 bar, and it already discarded locally feasible faster runs: E052 (4.99 s), E053 (5.07 s) and E046 (5.08 s). The new queue goes after that first.

**Gate work:**
- **H4.5.1 (priority 5):** three fresh builds of E049 on new seeds 33–52 to measure the rebuild SD. The same runs give E049's unselected population mean (H4.4.3).
- **H4.6.1 (priority 5):** freeze a gate before reading any result. Keep a candidate only if the mean minus 1.64 × the total SD is ≥0.75, with the total SD covering seed noise, rebuild noise and judge drift. Then test E052 and E053 on the fresh seeds. The fastest one that passes is confirmed once on reserved seeds 53–72 before it is kept again.
- **H4.2.6 (priority 4):** re-measures the epoch dial at no code cost. E049 minus 0.25 epoch is exactly E046, which is also a gate candidate.

**Cheap remaining levers:**
- **H1.8.1 (priority 3):** hierarchical label smoothing using the coarse labels, only if RULES.md allows them. This is a time-neutral structural booster.
- **H1.5.10 (priority 2):** BN-scale freeze, settled by reading the code first.
- **H2.6.11 (priority 2):** whitening detach moved from 20% to 6% of steps. This is a near-free cut, judged on per-step timing.
- **H7.1.1 (priority 2):** an offline run logging per-group update rates, to test whether "learning has finished" predicts which freezes are free.

I086 (ReLU, gated offline first) is still running. I dropped no queued ideas, because nothing else is queued. I deliberately left out tests for H1.2.2 (Muon vs SGD) and the H5 batch-size ideas: the committee forecast harm, and per-step overhead is only about 5%, so they would save little time.
